title: Tobit and the angel
hook: in a book kept in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, young Tobias travels with a stranger who is Raphael

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ezra and a weeping crowd sent off to feast, and your line was joy is your strength.

A young man needs a guide for a long trip, and the first person he meets is a friendly stranger who knows the road. They agree on a wage. The young man's mother cries as they leave, and the family dog trots along behind. That's the start of a journey in the book of Tobit. Catholic and Orthodox Christians count Tobit among the books of the Bible. Protestant churches don't count it as scripture, and some Protestant Bibles print it in a separate section called the Apocrypha. So depending on whose Bible is on the shelf, it's either there or it isn't.

Tobit is an Israelite in exile in Nineveh, a man who gives to the poor and, at real risk, buries the bodies of his people left in the street. One night he sleeps outside by a wall, sparrow droppings fall into his eyes, and he goes blind. Worn out and humiliated, he prays to die. The same day, far away, a young woman named Sarah prays the same thing. She's been married seven times, the story says, and each husband was killed by a demon on the wedding night. Two prayers of despair, and the book says both were heard, and the angel Raphael was sent to heal them both. Tobit, thinking he's near the end, sends his son Tobias to collect money he once left in trust with a man named Gabael. The guide Tobias hires says his name is Azarias. Along the road a great fish leaps out of the river at Tobias, and the guide tells him to keep its heart, liver and gall. Those drive the demon away from Sarah, whom Tobias marries, and heal Tobit's eyes back home. Only at the end, when the family tries to pay, does the guide say who he is: Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who stand before God. He was there, he says, when Tobit prayed and when he buried the dead. The help didn't arrive with wings. It walked the same dusty road as a hired companion, and nobody knew until the trip was over.
screen: `A BLIND MAN AND A GRIEVING BRIDE.`

segments.voice: Think of a trip in the day ahead, however short, a walk to the shops, a bus ride, a drive to an appointment, and someone who'd otherwise go alone or is nervous about where they're headed. Picture being good company on that road: matching their pace, carrying a bag, listening more than talking, staying until they arrive. If you pray, bring that person and that road before God; if you don't, just walk it once in your mind.
Raphael. The hired guide on Tobias's long journey, who turns out to be the angel sent to heal blind Tobit and rescue Sarah.
Your line: an angel on the road. Some help walks beside you unrecognized. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholic and Orthodox Christians read Tobit as scripture, and Catholics honor Raphael as an archangel with a feast day; Tobit is sometimes read at Catholic weddings. Protestant churches don't count it as scripture, though some Protestants read it among the Apocrypha.

notes: All of Tobit is paraphrased (no quotations), since KJV Apocrypha and Douay-Rheims wording differ and the writer was not certain of exact wording.

Canon description: Catholic and Orthodox include Tobit; Protestant churches do not count it as scripture, and 'some Protestant Bibles print it in a separate section called the Apocrypha'. Confirm wording is fair to all three.
'Seven times' (Sarah's husbands, Tobit 3:8) and 'one of the seven holy angels' (12:15) are from the text; numbering differs slightly between Greek recensions and Douay chapters. Confirm references.
The dog (5:16 / 11:4) differs in verse numbering between versions; confirm.
howItsDone mentions Raphael's feast day and Tobit read at Catholic weddings (Tobit 8 is an option in the Catholic wedding lectionary); confirm.
Original: רְפָאֵל; the name's meaning is deliberately not given (claims rule). Confirm pointing.

Editor pass: 'money the family left with a relative' corrected to money Tobit left in trust with Gabael (Tobit 1:14, 4:20); practice rewritten from noticing unseen help from others (too close to day 737's 'count the help on your side') to being a good companion on a short trip, the index practice.

Audit: teach said the guide was 'eating at the same fires'; in Tobit 12:19 Raphael says he did neither eat nor drink (they saw a vision), so changed to 'camping by the same river' (6:1). Trapdoor floor 1 ('angels show up shining') echoed day 737's trapdoor; replaced.
